To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the main limitation of the mass transfer in an electrophoresis-based membrane contactor is due to the interaction of the solute with the membrane surface.
the mass transfer is controlled by electrostatic interactions between the solute and the charged membrane.

(i) the mass transfer in electrophoretic separators is mainly governed by the electrostatic interactions at the membrane–buffer interface; and (ii) the mass transfer is limited by the electro-osmotic flow in the case of high buffer concentrations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of mass transfer phenomena in electrophoretic contactors.
the study of a new electroseparation technique which could be used for the separation and fractionation of macromolecules, in particular proteins.
the study of electro-separation processes in order to develop an electrophoretically-driven membrane contactor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mass transfer phenomena are governed by the electrostatic interactions taking part at the membrane–electrolyte interface, which are responsible of the solute partition coefficient.
electroseparation processes are limited by the electrostatic interactions taking part at the membrane–electrolyte solution interface.
the electroseparation processes are limited by the electrostatic repulsion of the charged groups of the solute and the membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mass transfer is controlled by electrostatic interactions at the membrane–liquid interface.
the mass transfer in an electrophoresis membrane contactor is mainly governed by electrostatic interactions taking places at the membrane–buffer interface.
the mass transfer in electrophoretic separators can be described by an equation similar to that used in conventional electrodialysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the electroseparation performances of an electroseparation process using an electrophoretically driven membrane contactor are mainly determined by the electrostatic interactions at the membrane–liquid interface.
it is possible to scale up electrosorption and electrodialysis processes by using an electrophoretically active membrane contactor.
the electroseparation process is mainly governed by the interactions at the membrane–buffer interface and the electroosmotic flow.
